summaryEn: Hoya learns who wrote down the words of Joseon kings and why even the king could not read their notes. A real 1404 entry from the Annals shows how faithfully they recorded.
hoyaIntroEn: How do we know what kings said long ago? Let's meet the people who wrote it all down!
hoyaOutroEn: The historians wrote it all down, day after day. Now you know where the Annals came from!
learningGoalsEn: Know that 사관 (sagwan) were royal historians who recorded what the king and officials said and did.
Know that the historians' draft notes, 사초 (sacho), were supposed to be kept secret, even from the king.
Understand the 1404 entry in which King Taejong asked that the historian not be told of his fall, and the historian recorded it anyway.
Know that the Annals (실록, sillok) cover 472 years and 25 kings, from Taejo to Cheoljong.
Read and recognize 기록 (girok), 사관 (sagwan), 사초 (sacho), 말 (mal) and 실록 (sillok).

scenes.narrationEn: Hoya the young tiger has a big question: how do we know what kings said hundreds of years ago? Because people wrote it down! In the Joseon kingdom, special officials recorded the work of the royal court every day.
scenes.captionEn: Hoya asks how we know what kings said
scenes.artBrief: A small friendly tiger cub sitting on a stack of old thread-bound books, head tilted with curiosity; warm hanji-paper background.

art.altEn: Hoya, a curious young tiger, stands by a stack of old thread-bound books and wonders how we know the past.

scenes.narrationEn: These officials were the {kw:sagwan}, the royal historians. Wherever the king met his officials, a historian was there, writing down what they saw and heard.
scenes.captionEn: A historian writes beside the king
scenes.artBrief: A Joseon palace hall: the king on a raised seat, officials kneeling in rows, and at the side a historian in official dress and a black hat writing with a brush on paper.

art.altEn: In a palace hall the king sits on a raised seat, officials kneel in rows and a historian at the side writes with a brush.

scenes.narrationEn: Joseon had eight full-time historians, and many other officials also served as part-time historians. Their notes were called {kw:sacho}, which means 'draft history.'
scenes.artBrief: Close-up of hands holding a calligraphy brush over sheets of handwritten paper, an inkstone and ink stick beside them.

art.altEn: A low desk holds a historian's handwritten draft notes beside an inkstone, an ink stick and a brush.

scenes.narrationEn: The rule was strict: no one was supposed to read the {kw:sacho}, not even the king. This helped the historians write fairly and protected their position.
scenes.captionEn: Not even the king may read them

line.en: Even the king was not allowed to read the sacho.
line.speaker: narrator

scenes.artBrief: A closed wooden document box tied with a red cord; the king, seen from behind, walking past it without opening it.

art.altEn: The king walks past a closed wooden box of the historians' notes, tied with a red cord, and leaves it shut.

scenes.narrationEn: One day in 1404, King Taejong went hunting. His horse stumbled, and he fell off. Luckily, he was not hurt!
scenes.captionEn: King Taejong falls from his horse
scenes.artBrief: A gentle countryside scene: a brown horse that has stumbled on grass, and a king in plain riding clothes sitting up on the ground, unhurt, brushing off his sleeve.

art.altEn: A brown horse grazes calmly in the green countryside where King Taejong went hunting in 1404.

scenes.narrationEn: Taejong looked around and said, 'Do not let the historian know!' But that very sentence is in the Annals today. The historian wrote down even this!

line.en: Do not let the historian know.
line.speaker: character

scenes.artBrief: The king glancing over his shoulder with a finger to his lips, while in the background a historian quietly writes; Hoya peeks from behind a tree, smiling.

art.altEn: The king looks around while a historian writes quietly in the distance, and Hoya peeks out from behind a pine tree.

scenes.narrationEn: The historians' notes became the most important source for the {kw:sillok}, the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty. The Annals cover 472 years and 25 kings, from Taejo to Cheoljong, and are on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register.
scenes.captionEn: The notes help make the Annals

keyword.en: the Annals (official history of each reign)

scenes.artBrief: A long row of old thread-bound books standing in a wooden case, with Hoya proudly pointing at them.

art.altEn: Hoya proudly waves beside a wooden case full of old books: the Annals, which record 472 years of Joseon kings.

facts.claimEn: In Joseon, royal historians (sagwan) wrote down the events of the royal court every day.
facts.claimKo: 조선의 사관은 궁중에서 일어난 일을 매일 기록하였다.

facts.claimEn: Historians attended wherever the king met his officials and recorded what they saw and heard.
facts.claimKo: 사관은 왕과 신하들이 자리하는 곳에 늘 참석하여 보고 들은 것을 기록하였다.
